entries.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
entries.abstract: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.
entries.comment: 8 pages, submitted to ECC27, this work is the first, foundational work that proposes Event-Centric Model Predictive Control (EC-MPC), a framework that combines model predictive control and neuromorphic control. Philosophy: predicting events but not trajectories; regulation without calibration

entries.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors
entries.abstract: In this letter, we consider trajectory tracking control and inertial parameter estimation of a quadrotor UAV whose center of mass (CoM) does not coincide with its geometric center. Onboard payloads like an IMU, a camera, or a battery are not necessarily placed at its geometric center. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset. Thus, these events and equipment introduce an offset and cause the inertia matrix to be non-diagonal. We develop an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online. We prove that the estimated parameters converge to their true values under a finite excitation condition. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using a simulation example.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. To be submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS) with the CDC 2027 option

entries.title: Ultrawideband Polarization-Rotating Antenna for Enhanced Ground Penetrating Radar Detection
entries.abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) represents a powerful and widely adopted tool for nondestructive subsurface detection and imaging. To overcome the impaired detection performance caused by polarization mismatch in conventional single-channel GPR systems, this paper presents an innovative ultrawideband polarization-rotating (UPR) antenna that achieves rotating linear polarizations (LPs) by varying the source frequency for enhanced detection. The developed UPR antenna achieves a continuous polarization rotation from 0° to 170° across 1.2 to 3.2 GHz, as verified by both full-wave simulations and experimental measurements. The antenna is subsequently integrated into a single-channel stepped-frequency GPR system and evaluated against targets of varying geometries in a sandy environment. Compared with a conventional fixed-LP GPR system, the UPR antenna-enabled GPR system delivers markedly more consistent detection performance across all target types, with particularly pronounced enhancements for polarization-sensitive targets. By enabling ultrawideband frequency-dependent polarization agility, the proposed GPR system enhances subsurface target detection while maintaining the simplicity and low cost of a single-channel measurement architecture.

entries.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
entries.abstract: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.

entries.title: Local Certificate Repair for Asynchronous Controller Updates in Recommender Systems
entries.abstract: We study how to adapt an existing distributed recommendation controller when local dynamics or objective weights change. Starting from a quadratic stability and cost certificate, we construct positive semidefinite corrections with finite spatial support and an explicit residual. A joint admission test allocates the available dissipation margin to these residuals and to interactions among changes and corrections, including pending updates. The test covers complete declared parameter ranges, allowing different operators to progress independently. For a fixed compatible batch, the corrections define a common storage that guarantees exponential stability and bounds the cost accumulated throughout deployment. When the admitted collection evolves, a reservation protocol preserves the certificate and a rate bound on storage increases ensures exponential convergence. Regional linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) design proposes new gain rows for the operators' own users, and a separate residual-based calculation can certify that the final gain lowers the expected cost. A recommendation-network example illustrates the tradeoff between repair depth, data access, and the benefits of deploying an update.

entries.title: A Distributed Observer with Random Agent Activations over Random Communication Networks
entries.abstract: This paper develops a distributed observer for the forward-Euler discretization of a continuous-time linear time-invariant system under random local operations and random communications. Under uniform stochastic strong connectivity, we establish almost sure exponential convergence of all local state estimates for sufficiently small discretization step sizes. We further examine how the underlying parameters and components affect the admissible range of the discretization step size and the guaranteed convergence rate bound. Unlike related approaches, the proposed method does not require each local unobservable subspace to admit an A-invariant complement.

entries.title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Transport Electrification for Low-Carbon Urban Planning: A Case Study of Phu Quoc, Vietnam
entries.abstract: Urban net-zero strategies require a defensible emissions boundary and quantitative estimates of the contribution achievable through individual mitigation measures. This study assesses road-transport electrification within a planned residential development in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, using the assumptions and scenario data of an urban-planning study originally prepared in 2022. A vehicle-class inventory combines population-dependent fleet projections, assumed travel activity, gasoline and diesel consumption, fuel-specific carbon dioxide (CO_2) factors, and electricity-related emissions from battery-electric vehicles. The reference case projects annual road-transport emissions of 59.41, 73.86, and 87.23 tCO_2 for 2022, 2025, and 2030, respectively. Three year-specific substitution scenarios, corresponding to nominal electric-vehicle shares of 25%, 50%, and 100%, yield source-reported avoided emissions of 9.43, 13.64, and 55.41 tCO_2/year, or 15.9%, 18.5%, and 63.5% of their respective baselines. However, a cross-scenario audit identifies an inconsistency in the 2025 mixed-fleet results under time-invariant vehicle-class emission-intensity ratios: under that additional assumption, 2025 avoided emissions would be 23.45 rather than 13.64 tCO_2/year. The original detailed vehicle-energy input tables are not included in the available source document, preventing definitive reconciliation. The study therefore provides a transparent, preliminary planning assessment rather than evidence of citywide net-zero attainment. Its principal value is a reproducible accounting structure and an explicit identification of the data, electricity-system, and infrastructure constraints that must be resolved before policy or investment decisions.

entries.title: GFM Control Automatic Compliance Toolbox
entries.abstract: The increasing penetration of converter-interfaced generation reduces system inertia, short-circuit strength, and voltage support. European grid codes, including the ENTSO-E Network Code on Requirements for Generators and the ACER Demand Connection Code, now define disturbance-based validation procedures for grid-forming (GFM) generation and converter-based demand. Commercial RMS tools, however, lack an integrated workflow aligned with these recent requirements. This paper presents an automated Python-PowerFactory compliance toolbox and an RMS test bench for a co-located system comprising a 1 MW GFM photovoltaic (PV) plant, a 0.3 MW GFM battery energy storage system (BESS), and a 1 MW converter-interfaced dynamic load at a 20 kV point of common coupling fed from a 110 kV grid. Extended virtual synchronous machine models and a DCC-oriented load model are tested in batch, with results automatically extracted and plotted for assessment. Results show compliant RMS performance for the slower, electromechanical tests, while the paper identifies which tests require complementary electromagnetic transient (EMT) verification.

entries.title: Grid-forming Control of Offshore Wind through a Diode-Rectifier HVDC System: a 2 GW Case Study
entries.abstract: Diode-rectifier-unit (DRU)-based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission considerably reduces the volume and weight of the offshore converter platform for remote wind farms and, hence, its cost, but shifts the task of forming and regulating the offshore AC network to the wind-turbine converters. This paper examines which grid-forming control strategy is the most suitable for DRU power transfer. The DRU commutation relationship shows that the delivered active power depends on the offshore voltage magnitude (but not on the converter voltage angle), so the angle-based active-power loop of virtual synchronous machine control is not closed through the rectifier. A P-V/Q-ω grid-forming architecture, which regulates active power via the voltage magnitude and derives frequency from the reactive power error, is therefore adopted. Electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1GWaggregated grid-forming turbine on a 66 kV collector network with a ±525 kV bipolar DRU link show that the commanded power is delivered over 800 to 1000MW with the offshore voltage held near nominal. The paper also examines how grid-forming operation changes the allocation of control duties within the Type-4 turbine: once the grid-side converter forms the network, DC link regulation must move to the machine-side converter, which limits the achievable bandwidth of the DC-link control. Extending the system to 2 GW with two 500 MW grid-following units achieves full power transfer in simulation, but with the grid-forming converter loaded beyond its continuous rating and a steady-state offshore frequency deviation of approximately 1.8 Hz.

entries.title: Spot Markets for AI Inference: Dynamic Capacity Allocation and Pricing on a Shared Accelerator Fleet
entries.abstract: Inference providers size their accelerator fleets for the interactive peak and sell spare capacity through fixed discounts, such as batch tiers at half price. However, inference differs from conventional cloud capacity in four respects: capacity depends on the latency tier through batching, moving weights between models is slow and costly, spot demand can wait until its deadline, and power can bind. In this paper, we develop a framework for dynamic capacity allocation and pricing of AI inference on a shared accelerator fleet. We consider a provider that serves several models under a power cap and sells each model in an interactive tier with a speed promise and in a spot tier for preemptible work with a deadline. In each period, the provider chooses how many replicas of each model to keep loaded and what spot price to quote. We show that one interactive token displaces a fixed number ρ_m>1 of spot tokens, and that the optimal spot price lies midway between the interactive price and the effective cost of capacity in the deadline window, which is close to the prevailing half price only when the fleet is slack. We further show that a spot tier raises the optimal reliability of the interactive tier, and that placement should follow persistent demand shifts while prices absorb transients. Building on these results, we design a model predictive controller based on a linear program with explicit approximation bounds, which solves each period in milliseconds. Numerical experiments on a simulated week with a measured daily demand profile, a flash crowd, and a grid curtailment show that the controller raises profit by 7.4% over fixed half-price practice, captures 93% of the gain available with perfect forecasts, keeps the interactive promise through both events, and leaves spot buyers better off.

entries.title: A Multistage Extension of Witsenhausen's Counterexample with Linear Signaling
entries.abstract: We study a multistage scalar extension of Witsenhausen's counterexample in which controller 1 observes the initial state exactly, whereas every subsequent controller observes only a local noise-corrupted state and does not inherit its predecessors' observations, so that every nonterminal action both regulates the state and shapes the signal available to the next controller. Restricting the signaling controllers to linear policies while leaving the terminal controller unrestricted, we compute the exact value within this class and reduce the optimization to a deterministic dynamic program in a single propagated variance. The optimal intermediate gains are shown to have a shrinkage form, and the value functions of that program are concave. For two stages, the benchmark admits a closed form on a matching locus, where for small effort weights it has two distinct minimizers, and at the standard parameter instance on that locus a two-point nonlinear policy strictly improves upon it. For three stages, numerical continuation at a reference instance reveals three distinct local minima, and two values of the initial variance at which the lowest of the three changes abruptly. Under the terminal-cost normalization we further prove, for every finite horizon, that the optimal linear value becomes asymptotically equal to the signaling-idle benchmark as the initial variance tends to infinity.

entries.title: Numerical Stability Issues and a Mitigation Method in Switching Events Calculation Considering State Variable Discontinuities for EMT Simulation
entries.abstract: Some existing methods for switching events calculation considering state variable discontinuities for EMT simulation can encounter numerical stability issues, either over-stabilizing or destabilizing the studied power systems. This paper documents these issues in detail with a concrete example. The underlying mechanism of the issues are revealed via systematic analysis. A mitigation method for the issues is proposed. The convergence behavior of the method is analyzed. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. It is observed that the method also helps to improve the accuracy of the simulation results.

entries.title: Learning the NMPC with Stability Guarantees
entries.abstract: Although nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) is widely used, its online optimization is computationally expensive. Neural network approximations of NMPC can effectively reduce the online computational burden but generally lack stability guarantees. This paper proposes an approximate NMPC framework with guarantees of constraint satisfaction and closed-loop stability. The approximation error is addressed through constraint tightening, and the resulting tightened NMPC is used to generate the training dataset of the approximate NMPC. The maximum allowable approximation error is prescribed a priori for the design of tightened NMPC and satisfied in a probabilistic sense through an iterative trial-and-error procedure alternating between network training and a posteriori verification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a numerical example of a constrained nonlinear system.
entries.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, this paper was not presented at any IFAC conference

entries.title: Analysis increments for model bias diagnosis and correction: Theoretical foundations
entries.abstract: A common method for diagnosing and correcting model bias in weather and climate prediction is based on analysis increments: the difference between the analysis and the forecast at each data assimilation cycle. Their time average is used to estimate and correct the bias, and machine learning is increasingly used to map the forecast state to the increments, giving a state-dependent correction. Despite its widespread use, the method lacks theoretical foundations. We first analyse a Kalman filter whose forecast model has a constant bias. We show what the averaged increment measures, and prove that iterating the correction removes all of the bias seen through the observations; for linear dynamics, no method can identify the rest. We then extend the analysis to state-dependent biases. For linear dynamics, each increment records the model error over the filter's memory, as seen through the observations. We use this to determine what the increments measure when averaged over a long period, averaged over periods with similar slowly varying conditions, and used without averaging, as in machine-learned corrections. Numerical experiments confirm the theory for a linear model and suggest that its main conclusions carry over to the nonlinear Lorenz '96 model, including for a correction learned by a neural network.

entries.title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
entries.abstract: Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems–monotonicity–can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only O(n) simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to 13,659 states and traffic networks with 1,000 states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.

entries.title: Feasibility-Aware Learning for Network-Constrained Unit Commitment
entries.abstract: Learning-based approaches to network-constrained unit commitment (NCUC) usually still rely on an optimization solver to repair or complete their predictions, which limits the speedup they can deliver. This paper proposes FALCON-UC, a feasibility-aware graph learning framework that predicts commitment and dispatch jointly and produces final schedules without solving a mixed-integer program at inference time. It combines an LSTM–GraphSAGE predictor over a fully connected generator graph, a differentiable correction that embeds commitment-dependent dispatch bounds, power balance, and PTDF-based branch flows in training, and deterministic commitment, dispatch, and ramp-coupled reserve repairs at inference. On the 2383-bus system, FALCON-UC achieves 99.09% commitment accuracy and a 0.4350% mean absolute cost gap with all evaluated constraints within tolerance at 0.0562 s per instance, a 2.27×10³ speedup over the solver. MTLR R-SCUC-FL is slightly more accurate but still needs an optimization solver to complete each schedule, which takes 262.2 s per instance, 4.67×10³ times the FALCON-UC runtime. A label-only baseline without repair violates the balance and branch limits on every 2383-bus test instance, and FALCON-UC also meets all evaluated constraint tolerances on a 1354-bus system.

entries.title: Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits
entries.abstract: Designing real-time control for nonlinear systems to track periodic orbits can be challenging, especially for complex and coupled dynamical systems (e.g., tethered kites), where the true model parameters are hard to obtain. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Koopman learning approach that incorporates periodic-orbit stability directly into the learned linear predictor. The approach combines the underlying periodic structure of the dynamics along with periodic state-input trajectory data to learn physically consistent linear predictors (in lifted/observable space). We leverage Floquet theory, which studies the stability of periodic orbits in nonlinear systems, to obtain the periodic stability information of a given orbit via a monodromy matrix (i.e., the state transition matrix over an entire period). Subsequently, we impose open-loop monodromy constraints to learn Floquet-parameterized linear predictors using a least-squares Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) formulation, thereby constraining the search space and aiding in Koopman learning. We then utilize these linear predictors to design a model predictive control (MPC) law for tracking periodic references. Finally, we evaluate the designed framework on a cartpole system under periodic forcing and compare it against a purely data-driven baseline.

entries.title: An Interline Multiport DC Circuit Breaker with Power Flow Controller
entries.abstract: Currently, the high-voltage multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids face two major challenges. First, fast rise rate and lack of zero-crossing point in DC-side fault currents render AC circuit breakers inoperable. Second, DC line currents are passively determined by terminal DC voltages and line resistances, which inherently limits the capability of changing individual line currents for essential grid services such as power flow management and overloading prevention. To address these two limitations, DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC power flow controllers (DCPFCs) have been developed. The conventional DCCBs are two-port devices installed in series with DC lines at their terminals in an MTDC converter substation, so that any fault current flowing through the line can be rapidly cleared. Additionally, a DCPFC can be installed at line terminals to adjust terminal voltages and power exchanges among adjacent lines. As a result, for a substation that connects to multiple lines, it needs to host multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, which significantly increases the cost and footprint of both the substation and the MTDC grid. To this end, this work proposes an integrated equipment combining multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, called the interline multiport DCCB with DCPFC, which can reduce the number of components and enhance the economic feasibility of MTDC networks. This paper presents the topology, operation principles, and component selection procedures of the proposed equipment, and compares it with the state-of-the-art technologies. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation results validate the fault interruption and power flow control performance of the interline multiport DCCB with PFC.

entries.title: BRACE: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control for Safe Navigation under Unknown Disturbances
entries.abstract: Disturbances encountered during autonomous navigation generally vary across space, often discontinuously, as obstacles redirect wind and changing terrain alters traction. Tracking controllers typically assume sufficient control authority to mitigate disturbances and maintain safety; the regime where this assumption fails remains underexplored. We present Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control (BRACE), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances. BRACE infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and uses that to condition a high-level policy that adapts the reference trajectory. The policy combines a nominal and a belief-guided residual term, trained jointly with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic. We evaluate BRACE in three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields, and validate it on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances. Across these settings, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance over model predictive control and RL baselines.

entries.title: Bisect-Index-Choose: A Fast and Exact Algorithm for EV Charging under Minimum Charging Rates
entries.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations are increasingly operated with an aggregate power limit below the sum of their port ratings, and require scheduling algorithms to divide the available power among the connected EVs. Charging standards permit a current that is either zero or at least a minimum rate, typically 6 A, which makes this allocation problem non-convex. Existing methods either solve a mixed-integer program with a commercial solver, which can be computationally expensive, adds software dependencies, and incurs licensing costs, or apply heuristics without optimality guarantees. This paper proposes Bisect-Index-Choose (BIC), a fast and solver-free scheduling algorithm that computes a globally optimal allocation among EVs under mild assumptions on their utilities. For n EVs, BIC runs in O(n logn) time when all EVs share one maximum rate and in O(n²) time for two, times a logarithmic factor in the numerical precision. In tests with up to 1000 EVs, BIC attains global optimality and is up to three orders of magnitude faster than the solver. On real-world charging data, it needs less capacity and delivers more energy than existing heuristics. We implement BIC on a low-cost microcontroller and show that it solves instances with 1000 EVs in less than 90 ms.

entries.title: Computationally Efficient Data Generation for Learning Nonlinear MPC Policies
entries.abstract: Learning MPC requires large datasets generated by repeatedly solving MPC problems. For Nonlinear MPC (NMPC), dataset generation is computationally expensive because feasible initial states are difficult to sample efficiently. The feasible set is often non-convex or even disconnected, and many randomly sampled states are infeasible, leading to wasted optimization solves and unnecessary computational effort. In this work, we propose a data-generation framework for learning NMPC policies that combines active-set exploration with projection-based sampling. First, a bilevel formulation samples activity weights to promote solutions associated with different active sets while preserving optimality for the original NMPC problem; second, a simpler slack-based formulation uses weighted slack variables to target different active sets at the single level. These reference solutions are then used to construct local linearized feasible sets, from which candidate initial states are sampled and projected through the nonlinear NMPC problem to recover feasible and locally optimal training samples. Our approach is up to 37× faster than baseline uniform sampling with 99% acceptance rate, while maintaining a representative coverage of the feasible set.

entries.title: Sampling-based Model Predictive Control as Sequential Monte Carlo Inference
entries.abstract: Sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) is treated as a family of distinct algorithms: predictive sampling, MPPI, the cross-entropy method, and their biased, colored-noise, and annealed variants all sample control sequences and reweight them by cost. We show a single Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference algorithm implements them all, specified by three independent axes: the proposal, the update rule that reduces cost-weighted particles to a nominal plan, and the effective-sample-size threshold for resampling. We evaluate SMC-based planning on MuJoCo non-linear control, open-loop navigation through obstacle fields, 7-DoF motion planning, and non-prehensile push-T, in simulation and on a Franka FR3. Resampling combats particle degeneracy at long horizons. At a 28-knot horizon in our navigation domain it cut the collision rate by 30% over non-resampling baselines. Programmable proposals improve push-T success over perturbative baselines, improving from 1% to 100% in simulation and 10% to 90% on hardware.
entries.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Code: https://github.com/CoMMALab/PFMP

entries.title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
entries.abstract: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient model is computationally prohibitive, whereas existing methods reduce the model to focus on a single timescale and lose accuracy when dynamics of different timescales interact. This paper proposes a nested heterogeneous multiscale framework for highly efficient multi-timescale simulation of a power system represented by one unified detailed model. Rather than varying only the integration step, the framework adaptively shifts the simulation resolution among three nested levels so that the dynamics of interest at each stage are always captured, with the slower dynamics estimated on the fly from short detailed simulations at controlled accuracy. Theoretical analysis proves the stability of long steps during quasi-steady-state evolution and quantifies the attainable speedup. On a modified IEEE 39-bus system with frequency regulation and load restoration, the framework accurately reproduces the dynamics of all timescales and runs 15 to 18 times faster than conventional simulation of the detailed model. The accuracy and speedup of the proposed method are further verified on a 390-bus system, demonstrating its scalability to large power systems.

entries.title: Modified CNN-Learned Surrogate Covariance With Krylov/Lanczos Subspace for DoA Estimation
entries.abstract: Recently, learning-based approaches have been employed to improve the robustness of subspace methods in DoA estimation. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was used as a data-driven framework employing an autoencoder to generate a well-conditioned surrogate covariance optimized end-to-end through a differentiable classical estimator, such as the Root-MUSIC. The complete system is designed to estimate the directions of arrival based on a spectral decomposition using the EVD of this covariance matrix. In this work, a new approach is proposed by formulating the spectral stage of the Root-MUSIC algorithm in terms of the orthogonal complement of the signal subspace, thereby eliminating the need for the noise subspace and noise eigenvalues. Furthermore, the full EVD is replaced by a Lanczos tridiagonalization with reorthogonalization, reducing the overall computational cost.

entries.title: Real-Time Threat Classification in Multi-Agent Systems via Topology-Coupled Hidden Markov Models
entries.abstract: Networked multi-agent systems coordinating in adversarial environments face compound cyber threats that alternate between false-data injection (FDI), denial-of-service (DoS), and stealthy decoy perturbations designed to mimic benign operational anomalies. Because the switching policy is latent and the plant dynamics evolve continuously, deterministic threshold detectors struggle to isolate deception without causing excessive false alarms. This paper presents an online, data-driven framework that couples distributed continuous time unknown input observers (UIOs) with a topology-aware Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for real-time attack detection and classification under unknown adversarial strategies. By decoupling FDI signals from augmented node states, distributed observers deployed across the network generate local augmented residuals that are discretized into emission sequences. The HMM embeds the underlying directed communication graph into the off-diagonal blocks of its transition probability matrix, explicitly capturing inter-agent attack propagation. Both transition and observation probabilities are updated recursively online via an Expectation-Maximization (EM) scheme, adapting the classifier to evolving threat behaviours without prior offline calibration. Numerical simulations on a directed network demonstrate that incorporating graph topology into the latent transition dynamics resolves the severe classification ambiguity between nominal and decoy modes, outperforming decoupled agent-independent decoders while restricting observer deployment to a sparse subset of nodes.

entries.title: Passivity-Guaranteed Variable Impedance and Compliance Control via Online Parameter Optimization
entries.abstract: Variable impedance control enhances the interaction capability of robot manipulators by adapting impedance parameters online. However, time-varying impedance parameters may inject energy into the system and violate passivity, particularly when tasks demand rapid stiffness changes. Existing methods address this by increasing damping or limiting the stiffness profile, which often degrades the dynamic response. In this work, we propose a quadratic programming-based parameter optimization framework that guarantees passivity by modulating the desired inertia to compensate for energy injected by stiffness variations, while preserving a critically damped system. For the case of diagonal impedance matrices, we optimize the rates of change of inertia and stiffness subject to a passivity constraint formulated as a convex quadratic program. We extend the framework to compliance control, where the desired inertia is coupled to the robot's configuration-dependent inertia matrix. We use an eigendecomposition based on Cholesky factorization to optimize the spectral weights while maintaining passivity. Experiments on the Kinova Gen3 7-degree-of-freedom manipulator validate both methods with human interaction perturbations. Comparisons with an energy tank approach and a nonpassivity-based method demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves less conservative stiffness tracking without requiring an energy reservoir or damping overhead.

entries.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Massively Parallel Simulation for Low-Thrust Multi-Revolution Rendezvous
entries.abstract: The growing demand for on-orbit servicing and constellation management in low Earth orbit requires autonomous and reliable low-thrust rendezvous. Traditional numerical methods struggle with the long-horizon nature of multi-revolution maneuvers under perturbations, while standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods are limited by low simulation throughput and poor sample efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a massively parallel DRL guidance framework. A fully tensorized, GPU-resident orbital propagator is developed to integrate J₂-perturbed orbital dynamics and policy optimization within a zero-copy pipeline, achieving up to a 67-fold increase in simulation throughput over conventional CPU baselines. In addition, the rendezvous problem is formulated in modified equinoctial elements and trained with a progressive curriculum learning strategy to improve convergence and generalization across increasingly challenging rendezvous scenarios. Simulations show that the proposed framework can learn robust rendezvous trajectories for complex multi-revolution rendezvous over a broad range of orbital configurations. Additional evaluations under a high-fidelity model and eclipse-induced thrust interruptions further demonstrate the robustness of the learned policy under practical mission constraints. Moreover, the trajectories generated by the proposed framework can be used as effective initial guesses for optimization-based trajectory solvers, improving the convergence of high-precision trajectory optimization. The method offers a scalable approach for real-time low-thrust guidance and trajectory optimization.

entries.title: Two-Timescale Trajectory Control, Task Reassignment and Resource Scheduling for Multi-UAV Cooperative Mobile Edge Computing
entries.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) is a promising technology, leveraging the advantages of UAVs including flexible deployment, wide coverage, and reliable wireless communication. In this paper, we study the task reassignment and offloading problem in a multi-UAV cooperative operating environment, and consider the real occurrence that the computing tasks arrive more frequently than UAVs make flight decisions. In addition, we also take into account the position offset of the UAV during flight and the unavailability of the UAV due to external interference. We propose a two-timescale optimization framework, where the trajectory of the UAV is carried out on a large timescale, while the task reassignment and computing resource allocation are jointly optimized on a small timescale. The core objective is to maximize the long-term average system gain, which takes both energy consumption and task delay into account. To address the UAV trajectory optimization problem under large timescale constraints, we propose a constrained multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm. For decision-making within small timescale, to jointly optimize task offloading decisions and computing resource allocation, we integrate convex optimization with a heuristic algorithm. Finally, we conduct extensive simulations to evaluate the proposed algorithms against the baseline, achieving a 24% reduction in latency and a 28% reduction in total system cost.

entries.title: Worst-Case Contagion in Financial Networks: MILP Clearing and Robust Loss Analysis
entries.abstract: We study worst-case contagion losses in financial networks with interbank liabilities and common exposures to marketable assets. Existing linear-programming approaches provide exact stress-test values only within an insolvency-resilience margin, where all institutions remain solvent with respect to the external sector. We show that this margin is computed exactly by a finite family of linear programs, one per vertex of the uncertainty ball, whereas a single linear program based on the componentwise worst deterioration of external resources yields only a certified lower bound. We extend this framework beyond that margin in three directions. First, we derive an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the maximal clearing vector under arbitrary signed external net positions, providing a clearing oracle for robust stress testing when insolvency can occur. Second, we develop certified bounds on the worst-case loss beyond the margin, including insolvency-pattern enumeration, scenario lower bounds, fixed-pattern dual upper bounds, localized certificates, and a regime-generation procedure with monotone gap certificates. Third, we analyze the worst-case loss curve as a function of the perturbation radius. For ℓ₁ and ℓ_∞ price-perturbation sets, the curve is convex, nondecreasing and piecewise linear up to the margin, with breakpoints generated by switches in worst-case shock directions, LP bases, and bank-level activity patterns. Beyond the margin, it remains nondecreasing and piecewise affine, but convexity may fail, the curve may jump upward, and the worst case need not be attained. The framework provides a certifiable MILP/LP methodology for parametric stress testing and interpretable diagnostics identifying the banks responsible for changes in systemic loss.

entries.title: From Discrete Snapshots to Geometric Entity: Motion-Native Channel Tracking for THz Near-Field XL-MIMO
entries.abstract: Channel tracking in mobile terahertz (THz) near-field extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems is challenging because spherical-wave propagation couples angle and range, leading to rapid and nonlinear channel evolution under sparse pilot observations. Existing approaches typically estimate pilot-local channel or position snapshots before applying temporal tracking or smoothing, making them vulnerable to information loss during snapshot formation. To break this bottleneck, we propose a paradigm shift from tracking discrete snapshots to estimating a holistic geometric entity, namely, one shared continuous UE trajectory over the tracking window. Specifically, we parameterize the trajectory using a low-dimensional cubic B-spline representation and directly couple the per-pilot profile likelihoods through this shared trajectory before any pilot-local position estimate is finalized, thereby inducing continuous near-field channel evolution. We further characterize the efficient geometric information supplied by each pilot observation and its aggregation in the shared spline-coefficient space. Based on this formulation, we develop a regularized maximum a posteriori estimator and a quadratic-penalty lifted solver that separates parallel pilot-local geometric updates from a structured global spline update. The resulting global system is banded and, for a fixed spline degree, admits linear-complexity factorization, enabling an efficient structured implementation. Simulations demonstrate consistently improved tracking accuracy over representative temporally refined baselines in the tested medium-to-high-SNR regime, together with a favorable accuracy–runtime trade-off. These results highlight the benefit of coupling sparse pilot observations through a shared continuous trajectory rather than temporally processing independently estimated snapshots.

entries.title: Shifted Interaction Functions: A Unified Framework for Imperfect Actuation and Sensing in Consensus Networks
entries.abstract: Practical networked robotic systems rarely implement ideal consensus interactions exactly, since local actuation constraints, sensing biases, and heterogeneous interaction maps may shift the input-output relations used by distributed controllers. Rather than focusing solely on whether consensus occurs, such imperfections can fundamentally alter the structure of the asymptotic collective behavior, typically yielding global or clustered velocity alignment, while exact static agreement arises only in special cases. This paper develops a shifted-interaction framework for analyzing collective alignment under imperfect actuation and sensing. Shifted functions provide a compact representation of local actuator and sensor maps, allowing actuation constraints and sensing biases to be represented by horizontally and vertically shifted monotone interactions. The framework distinguishes nodal shifted actuation from edge-wise shifted sensing. For shifted actuation, a Lyapunov analysis establishes global velocity alignment under compatible actuation ranges, including bounded, non-invertible, and deadzone-type maps. For shifted sensing, a maximum-principle argument and a paired-sensitivity condition establish convergence to velocity clusters over edges with infinite accumulated sensitivity; uniform sensing sensitivity yields exponential global velocity alignment. In the linear case, closed-form expressions characterize asymptotic behavior and identify actuation as a special case of sensing. Simulations illustrate static, globally aligned, and clustered velocity-aligned behaviors.

entries.title: Online Geometric Consistency Assessment of LiDAR Measurements via Recursive Bayesian Comparison
entries.abstract: LiDAR-based localization and mapping systems produce registered point clouds that serve as geometric measurements for downstream estimation and navigation. Registration errors introduce duplicated surfaces and structural deformation into these measurements. In the absence of an independent reference, online assessment relies on geometry accumulated from earlier measurements. Such assessment requires tolerance to sampling variation and an accumulation process in which observations enter the history only after evaluation. We therefore formulate a recursive Bayesian comparison that couples geometric assessment with history maintenance. A Normal-Inverse-Wishart model represents historical voxel geometry and its uncertainty, while a weak isotropic reference adapts to current sampling. Comparing the marginal predictive support of the same current points under both models yields Normalized Drift Evidence (NDE). Assessment precedes assimilation: positive NDE triggers an alarm and preserves the preceding historical state; otherwise, the current observations update the history. Across 14 real-world sequences totaling approximately 73 min from four platform types, alarms identified all nine corrupted sequences and were absent from all five consistent sequences. In four representative scenarios with event references, first alarms occurred within 0.9 s of the reference times, with no preceding alarms. Cross-backend evaluation demonstrates consistent responses to reconstructed geometry. Ablation and controlled perturbation results establish the roles of uncertainty modeling, recursive history, displacement, and geometric support. Mean processing time is 4.2–6.1 ms per update at 1 Hz. In ten UAV trials, alarms initiated odometry isolation, landing, relocalization, and mission continuation.

entries.title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
entries.abstract: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system state. In contrast, the integrity attacker in this study replaces the sensor measurements with fabricated data to drive the system to undesired operating conditions. Although these two threats are typically studied separately, a wireless NCS should be protected against both simultaneously, and a defence against one affects the other. We employ an observation-encoding scheme that renders the eavesdropper's state-estimation error covariance unbounded under packet drops, and show that transmission energy governs how long this error remains bounded. In particular, lower transmission energy improves confidentiality. For integrity protection, we combine stochastic physical watermarking with a CUSUM-based sequential change detector. The proposed attack detection scheme accounts for intermittent communication and encoded measurements. The detection delay is governed by the Kullback–Leibler divergence (KLD) between the pre- and post-attack distributions of the test signal, and we show that a higher transmission energy increases the KLD and thereby reduces the detection delay. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the eavesdropper's estimation error and the worst-case expected KLD, providing guidelines for selecting transmission energy to balance confidentiality and integrity protection and characterising the privacy–security trade-off. Finally, we run numerical simulations to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the privacy–security trade-off in practical scenarios.

entries.title: On Real Eventual Exponential Positive property of complex-valued Laplacians and their pseudoinverses
entries.abstract: The property of real eventual exponential positivity guarantees the state trajectories of a linear time-invariant system to evolve asymptotically to right half of the complex-plane [1]. It has applications in the characterization of herdability and reachability of states in networked systems. Networks with complex-valued edge-weights arise in AC power systems and opinion dynamics. Recent work has introduced real eventual exponential positive (rEEP) Laplacians, for which the trajectories of the associated network flow eventually converge to consensus. We establish further properties of rEEP Laplacians and their pseudoinverses. Firstly, we show that the rEEP property for complex-valued matrices exhibits invariance under specific rotational transformations. Secondly, we establish that the property of rEEP is preserved under the MoorePenrose pseudoinverse operation, highlighting its robustness under algebraic manipulations. These results apply to effective impedance computation in AC networks and to consensus in multi-agent systems. Finally, we provide numerical examples to validate our theoretical results.

entries.title: Dynamic State Estimation from Sparse PMUs via Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operators
entries.abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph neural operator for power system dynamic state estimation. From a sparse, intermittent measurement window at a few generator buses, the operator estimates the rotor-angle and speed trajectories of all machines, unmeasured ones included, in one forward pass. A graph-attention encoder processes the measurements, and the swing equations are imposed as a hard constraint or as a soft one with a learned correction that absorbs model errors. It is trained on simulated measurements, without state labels. With several phasor measurement units, masked training hides one from the input but keeps it in the loss. On four transmission systems, simulations show that the operator is the most accurate estimator that neither optimizes per scenario nor uses state labels, except on the smallest system at large model errors, where tuned Kalman smoothers are better. Networks trained on simulated states are more accurate on the two smallest systems but not on the 118-bus system, where the operator is faster and more accurate than hard-constrained moving-horizon estimation. Under model errors, it matches or outperforms an optimization-based benchmark at a fraction of its cost. The results hold for a detailed machine model with exact parameters seen only through voltage phasors.

entries.title: Simulating Nonlinear Resistive Networks using a Behavioral Splitting
entries.abstract: An operator splitting method is developed for computing operating points of nonlinear resistive networks. Our behavioral formulation separates the device laws from Kirchhoff's laws and casts simulation as a zero-finding problem. Branch port resistances then provide a diagonal preconditioner for the relaxed Peaceman-Rachford iteration in scattering variables. Each iteration requires solving independent scalar equations and a linear system with a fixed weighted Laplacian matrix. Convergence is established for maximal monotone device laws when an operating point exists. Contractive branch reflections also yield a linear convergence bound independent of network topology. Numerical experiments on crossbar arrays illustrate the computational advantages.

entries.title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design
entries.abstract: Multiple robots operating in shared workspaces must adjust their speed, direction, and trajectories to coordinate with one another and respond to changing tasks and disturbances. The available maneuver freedom depends on the dynamics, uncertainty, and safety margins, even for a fixed fleet size and workspace. However, robot count, workspace occupancy, and task throughput do not quantify how much the fleet can vary its motion or how reliably these variations can be observed. We develop a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that jointly characterizes these two aspects. Mobility information is defined as the mutual information between a joint maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation, and MIC maximizes this quantity under maneuver-resource constraints. For a linear Gaussian maneuver-to-observation model with feedback dynamics, we characterize the finite-horizon information benchmark and derive its stationary long-horizon spectral limit, accounting for heterogeneous mobility gains, colored uncertainty, and temporally coupled maneuver costs. We further map workspace-boundary, inter-robot separation, and actuator chance constraints into coupled maneuver-covariance restrictions and derive conditions under which covariance optimization reduces to resource allocation across mobility modes. Finite joint maneuver codebooks are then constructed through individual risk screening and noise-whitened trajectory separation, with bounds linking sequence recovery error and achieved information to the capacity benchmarks. An aerial-robot simulation study evaluates spectral convergence, safety-aware allocation, finite-codebook identification, and fleet-size scaling. The resulting framework complements occupancy and task-throughput measures by quantifying the maximum observable maneuver freedom supported by a mobility system.

entries.title: Maze Runner: Autonomous Maze Navigation with Line-Based Localization and Control Barrier Functions
entries.abstract: Maze navigation requires localization from sparse, repetitive geometry, planning through narrow corridors, and control that stays safe when the estimate or the map is wrong. We present Maze Runner, an open autonomy stack in C++ and ROS 2 that addresses these needs end to end on a simulated Husarion ROSbot XL with a 2D LiDAR in Gazebo. Perception extracts wall lines from each scan with RANSAC and total least squares, with per-line uncertainty. The same line front end feeds two estimators: an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that localizes against a line map built from the maze mesh, and an EKF SLAM variant that builds the line map online. Planning runs online on an inflated occupancy grid with A* plus line-of-sight shortcutting, or with a forward-only Hybrid A*. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) tracks the plan while discrete-time Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) on world-frame LiDAR points keep the robot clear of walls and unmapped obstacles. The algorithms live in a ROS-free, unit-tested core library, and the whole stack builds and runs from a single reproducible environment. In simulation, the robot drives a 135 m route through the maze with 1.0 cm localization RMSE against the known map and 24 cm in SLAM mode, the planner returns a path in 6 ms, and the NMPC solves in 11.7 ms on average, never exceeding its 80 ms budget.

entries.title: Dynamic Traffic Modeling using Equivalent Circuit Models
entries.abstract: This paper presents an equivalent circuit model (ECM) for dynamic traffic modeling by exploiting analogies between electrical and transportation variables. Vehicle concentration is represented by capacitor voltage, while traffic flow is modeled using controllable current sources. The proposed formulation is shown to preserve the conservation and sending/receiving relationships of the spatially discretized Lighthill Whitham Richards traffic model. The framework is extended to restricted inflow, traffic signals, and two road merging and diverging scenarios. Validation against microscopic Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulations, involving traffic signals, two-road merging, and single-road diverging scenarios, demonstrates that the proposed ECM successfully reproduces the principal macroscopic traffic dynamics, including queue formation, backward congestion propagation, vehicle accumulation, saturation, and subsequent traffic recovery.

entries.title: Agibot: An Open-Source Modular Swerve-Drive Robot Platform for Agricultural Robotics Research and Education
entries.abstract: Agricultural production faces persistent labor shortages and increasing demand for automation, yet progress in agricultural robotics remains constrained by the limited availability of affordable, flexible, and accessible research platforms. This paper presents Agibot, an open-source, modular, low-cost agricultural robotics platform designed for autonomy research and experimentation, with potential applications in hands-on robotics education. The platform integrates four-wheel independent swerve drive, swappable computing, distributed embedded control, multimodal sensing, and configurable manipulation within a unified sense-plan-act-verify framework supporting perception, control, navigation, manipulation, and autonomous task verification. The platform was evaluated through representative row-crop navigation and manipulation tasks under varying lighting and soil conditions. Experiments demonstrated reliable lane following, autonomous row-to-row navigation, target identification, seed dispensing, plant manipulation, and closed-loop verification of task success. Its modular architecture supports independent testing, modification, and validation of autonomy components for rapid prototyping and experimentation. These proof-of-concept tasks, controller-tuning studies, and integrated trials demonstrate the platform's research capabilities, while its accessible and reconfigurable design supports its use for hands-on robotics education. By combining affordability, modularity, open-source accessibility, configurable manipulation, and end-to-end sense-plan-act-verify autonomy, Agibot provides a practical platform for agricultural robotics research, technology development, and workforce training.

entries.title: Sample-Covariance Regularization for Data-Driven Predictive Control from Frequency Response Functions under Colored Noise
entries.abstract: In this work, we investigate how sample covariance obtained from frequency-response functions (FRFs) can be exploited to improve performance of data-driven frequency-domain predictive control (FreePC) in the presence of colored measurement noise. In case of periodic multisine excitation, this covariance is obtained directly from repeated periods and provides a frequency-dependent measure of uncertainty without requiring an additional parametric noise model. To incorporate this information into both indirect and direct predictive control, we develop a frequency-domain subspace predictive controller (FD-SPC) and establish its equivalence to the direct FreePC formulation in the noiseless setting. Regularization terms for both formulations are then motivated by expected prediction-error criteria and constructed from the sample covariance of the FRF estimates. Across all tested noise models and data sizes, regularization consistently reduces the median realized control cost relative to the corresponding controller without covariance regularization, with reductions of up to 35%.

entries.title: Control of Linear Dynamical Systems with Operational Constraints
entries.abstract: This paper presents a method for designing servo-controllers that enforce operational constraints on multi-input multi-output linear time-invariant dynamical systems. The proposed method introduces a control augmentation that complements a baseline controller to ensure forward invariance of state/output trajectories within prescribed box constraints. The derivations of the control design are based on the Nagumo Theorem, the Comparison Lemma, and principles from min-norm optimal control akin to the theory of Control Barrier Functions. Importantly, an explicit piecewise-linear feedback control law is derived, which provides continuous enforcement of constraints without online optimization, enabling rigorous stability and robustness analysis via classical linear systems theory. Extensions to handle estimation errors in output feedback and integral action in proportional-integral control are provided. Theoretical results are validated through flight control simulation studies that demonstrate input/output constraint satisfaction, robustness to disturbances, and closed-loop stability. The proposed method offers a mathematically rigorous, practical, and analyzable alternative to common heuristic or optimization-intensive constrained control strategies.

entries.title: Open-Source Multi-Fidelity EMT Modeling of Data Center Loads for Power System Studies
entries.abstract: Characterizing data center-grid interactions under rapid load fluctuations requires electromagnetic transient (EMT) models that capture fast converter and control dynamics. This paper develops a modular multi-fidelity EMT model of data center loads in PSCAD. The modular design supports flexible assembly of subsystem models for different power supply configurations. The multi-fidelity design incorporates switching models, average-converter models, and reduced-order models to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency according to analysis needs. The model also provides a systematic controller tuning procedure and supports control mode switching. Comparative simulations demonstrate how this data center load model responds to both grid-side and load-side disturbances and assess the accuracy and computational efficiency of models with three fidelity levels. The model is publicly available on GitHub.

entries.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
entries.abstract: This paper presents a deterministic geometric procedure for analysing affine constraints over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by chance-constrained set approximation. Analytical tests classify inequalities as always violated, never violated, or cutting. Pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be strictly violated at a common point, yielding a compatibility matrix. The tests follow from quadratic optimisation and the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions, with explicit treatment of tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate inequalities. The formulation applies in arbitrary finite dimensions and provides geometric information for subsequent bounds on simultaneous sampled violations and safe-region approximation.
